entry.summary: Sentencing of Mr Richards (as principal) and Mr Haenga (as a party) for the murder of Hori Gage. Sentence of life imprisonment imposed for both offenders. Section 104(1)(e) engaged. For Mr Richards, a minimum period of imprisonment (MPI) under s 103 would be 17 years, reduced by six months to account for personal factors. In the circumstances, an MPI of 17 years would not be manifestly unjust and reflects the seriousness and callousness of the offending, and the significance of the need for deterrence. Mr Richards sentenced to life imprisonment with an MPI of 17 years. For Mr Haenga, an MPI under s 103 would be 14 years, reduced by one year to account for personal factors. In the circumstances, and given Mr Haenga's significantly lesser culpability, it would be manifestly unjust to impose a 17-year MPI. Mr Haenga sentenced to life imprisonment with an MPI of 13 years.
